title: What will ticket arrangements be for Rangers v Celtic in Scottish League Cup? - bbc.com
content: Police create cordon on pitch to separate Old Firm fans As soon as the draw was completed for the Scottish League Cup quarter-finals, some big questions arose for clubs and supporters alike, particularly for followers of Glasgow's big two, pitted against each other in a powder keg tie. Given what happened the last time Rangers and Celtic met in a cup competition, how can match safety and security be guaranteed? What chance is there that Celtic could be given a whole stand at Ibrox, as they were in March? And, perhaps most intriguingly of all, how many tickets are Rangers obliged to give their rivals? Rangers thump League Cup holders St Mirren for McInnes' first win Clinical Celtic into last eight after beating wasteful Dundee Utd Theoretically, Celtic could be offered next to no visiting tickets for the match at Ibrox - at least according to the rules and regulations set out by the Scottish Professional Football League for their primary cup competition. For confirmation of this, BBC Scotland took a deep dive into the books. The relevant information is listed in Annex 2 - The Scottish Professional Football League Cup Competition Regulations - and section 11, Admission Arrangements for Visiting Clubs and clubs. This is where it becomes clear that, in theory at least, Rangers are only required to make 50 tickets available to Celtic - 10 for the directors' box and 40 for the stand, as detailed in sub-section one: "11.1 The Home Club shall forward to the Visiting Club 'without charge' tickets, in the numbers set out below, so that they will be in the hands of the Visiting Club on or before the fifth day before the Match (unless under circumstances which render this impracticable) - 10 for Directors' Box, 40 for the Stand." Further to this, the only other official stipulation in the competition guidelines that applies to tickets (at least up to and including the quarter-final stage) is in the next section of the rulebook: "11.2 No Official or Player of the Visiting Club shall be entitled to enter the Home Club's Ground without a ticket." It would therefore appear to be within Rangers' gift, according to the strictest reading of the rules, to have very few Celtic supporters at Ibrox. Despite what's written in the rules, there's also an element of custom and practice to these things. Especially, as with this derby, the high profile nature of the match and the desire from broadcasters, sponsors and neutral observers to have the best possible atmosphere in the ground. What clubs tend to do in the League Cup is operate along the parameters of the arrangements already in place for league matches, namely: "The Home club must make provision for the admission of such reasonable number of visiting supporters at every home League Match and Play-Off Match as may be agreed in advance with the Visiting Club and, in the event of their being unable to agree such number not later than 14 days prior to the date of the League Match or Play-Off Match in question, the number of visiting supporters allowed shall be determined by the Board whose decision shall be final and binding." This "reasonable number" has been a hot topic with Celtic and Rangers for quite some time now. After a period in which both clubs declined entry to away fans, a compromise figure of roughly 5% of the respective grounds was arrived at, which has meant about 2,500 away fans have been present at Premiership Old Firm games across the past couple of years. It's highly likely this will be the kind of allocation Celtic can expect as they go head to head with Ranges for a place in the semi-finals. The ugly scenes that followed Celtic's Scottish Cup win over Rangers at Ibrox in March made headlines and led to an independent inquiry, which criticised both clubs and virtually every aspect of the tie from an operational and safety standpoint. Celtic and Rangers both face charges and the review concluded that "a violent mass confrontation" was only narrowly avoided after a number of spectators from both sides went on to the pitch after Martin O'Neill's side won a penalty shootout to reach the semi-finals. Celtic supporters had been given the whole of the Broomloan Stand, the traditional away end at Ibrox, in line with Scottish Cup rules that allow for a larger allocation of tickets to the visiting club. The chances of 7,500 away fans at either ground in future now appear remote after the near-carnage witnessed that day when fireworks were thrown and multiple arrests were made. The short answer to that is very soon, given the match itself is scheduled for the weekend of 12 September. Supporters should know within a day or two which matches have been picked up for live broadcast, with Rangers v Celtic certain to be the jewel in the television crown for the quarter-finals. That will determine the date and time of the fixture. As for the ticket arrangements? Both Rangers and the SPFL say it's far too soon to make any comment, given the draw was only made on Sunday. There may also be some negotiating to be done to ensure both clubs are happy with any proposed arrangements and avoid the final decision on numbers being taken out of their hands entirely. title: Gov. Lombardo orders flags lowered on Monday to honor Christopher V. Andersen of Lake Tahoe - Carson Now
content: Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo has ordered flags to be lowered to half-staff on Monday, August 17, 2026, in honor of the life and service of U.S. Forest Service-contracted helitack aerial firefighting pilot Christopher V. Andersen. On August 7, Andersen made the ultimate sacrifice while supporting aerial firefighting operations on the Widemouth 2 Fire near Three Creeks Reservoir in Fishlake National Forest, Utah. “Christopher V. Andersen dedicated more than four decades of his life to aviation and public service, first as a helicopter pilot in the U.S. Army and later flying critical missions and protecting communities across the country and around the world,” said Gov. Lombardo. “Mr. Andersen made his home near Lake Tahoe, where he served as a chief pilot and mentor and earned the respect of fellow aviators for his skill, leadership, and professionalism. His courage, service, and dedication to protecting others will not be forgotten by the people of the State of Nevada.” The flag order applies to the Nevada State Capitol and all state public buildings and grounds from sunrise to sunset on Monday, August 17, at the request of Mr. Andersen’s family. title: VMAN 57: Fall in line With Paul Anthony Kelly - V Magazine
content: Though he came to fame playing John F. Kennedy, Jr. in Ryan Murphy’s unmissable Love Story, the actor is excited for what’s next—and there’s a lot to look forward to Though he came to fame playing John F. Kennedy, Jr. in Ryan Murphy’s unmissable Love Story, the actor is excited for what’s next—and there’s a lot to look forward to To deem Paul Anthony Kelly a newcomer seems entirely incongruous with his on-screen charisma. After spending over a decade learning how to tell a story through a still image—modeling for everyone from Loro Piana to Brooks Brothers—he finally nabbed the role of John F. Kennedy Jr. in FX’s Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette, his first official acting credit after doggedly auditioning for years. Tall and strapping with a dimpled smile, Kelly harkens back to the movie stars of classic Hollywood, keenly comfortable on camera without sacrificing his tenacious undercurrent. Millions of Americans met Kelly on tablets, TVs, and laptops earlier this year, when his roguish portrayal of one of America’s most enduring sex icons cemented him as much more than “a pretty face,” in the words of the inimitable Niecy Nash. Indeed, Kelly will join Kirsten Dunst and Sydney Sweeney on screen in The Housemaid’s Secret, arriving next year. And amidst his shooting schedule for the 13th season of American Horror Story, Kelly sat down with Niecy Nash, another member of Ryan Murphy’s ever-expanding universe, to chat about breaking the mold, bringing true love to the screen (in two ways), and a shared love of villainy. NIECY NASH: I often say that people want to leave you where they meet you: I know you to do this thing, and they put a pin in it, not understanding that you can be multifaceted. I had to get to a place where I had a team that saw me the way I saw myself and knew that I could pull from a deeper well. And once I was able to do so, that’s when I started getting nominations. Was that similar for you, Paul? PAUL ANTHONY KELLY: Yeah, I always knew that I wanted to do this. I knew that I was capable of it. It took a long time for people to buy it, essentially. PAK: I don’t know. I was a model for a long time, and that kind of comes with the stigma. PAK: You said it, not me. But yes, exactly. People don’t take you seriously. NN: Now it’s a delicious double dip. You are a pretty face, but you also have the chops to back it up. PAK: Thank you. See, I always knew that. So, now it’s nice to rub it in the proverbial face a little bit. It’s freeing, for me, breaking the shackles of the modeling world. I’m just along for the ride in my own little world here that I’m holding for myself. I’ve already done the work that’s meaningful to me, and now I have opportunities to do more meaningful work. NN: Okay, let me act like I know what I’m doing. So let me ask you, what do you feel like modeling taught you about being an actor? PAK:  Body movement, definitely. I think being a model for so long got me very comfortable in front of a camera, and there is something to telling a story in a two-dimensional image where you still have to emote. I think that really helped with getting myself into a place of understanding the nuances of life, as it were. But then being able to live it and express it fully as an actor in front of a moving camera. I think that helped a lot. NN: Now, because you had so many eyes on this project, has it changed out in the wild when you are trying to go get a cup of coffee or when you are at the bookstore perusing the shelves? PAK: A little bit. I’m still in that crossover phase of recognition. When I’m out in the wild, I don’t look like John. Typically I’m more bearded than I am now. I wear glasses, I have a hat on, and I’m a little scruffy sometimes. A lot of people are like, ‘is that—maybe not, can’t be.’ But it has been happening more often that people are noticing me, and I kind of love it. The reception has been so overwhelmingly positive. I think people really resonate with my story as well. It took me so long to get this opportunity, and then I did it to the best of my ability, and I think I did a really good job. I’m proud of the work I did, and people are also proud of that. It just hearkens back to perseverance, and if you truly want something, then go and get it. I think people resonate with that. NN: When you play a lover, how does it fare—because you’re married, right? PAK: That’s correct. My wife was on set pretty much every day, too. I mean, there were certain days and scenes that she was like, ‘I don’t need to be here for that.’ But I’m so incredibly lucky to have such a wonderfully supportive and caring and understanding partner in all of this. She’s always known that this was my dream. When I got this role, as soon as I got it, we were in New York, Sarah [Pidgeon] was like, ‘I have to meet your wife first before we do this.’ They really hit it off right away, and it was nice of Sarah to push for that, and to create this understanding and friendship and bond before we went in and did this. I think [Sarah and I] had pretty great professional chemistry, but there were a lot of things from my own relationship that I brought into this. I couldn’t have done it without knowing the love I know with my wife. NN: I know that’s right. Where do you go from here, or where do you aspire to go from here? PAK: Oh my gosh, the list is long. There have always been stories that I would like to tell or retell or have a hand in telling. This was a really amazing thing that I was gifted from the universe, and of course also from Mr. Ryan Murphy and his team for seeing something in me that no one else really did. He just has this thing where he sees something in you and wants to see you find it in yourself and explore it. While Love Story was being released, he called me about [American Horror Story]. PAK: I’m filming that now. With John Jr., I feel like I just tried to stay within the ethos of him and the aura and energy of it, and still kind of make it mine. But this other character that I’m doing now in Horror Story, it’s totally different already. I have such free rein, and it’s such a gift to just be able to play and figure out who these characters are in your head and in your body. NN: One thing I can say is that Ryan Murphy is a gift to actors. He gives you things that are so delicious on the page, you cannot wait to unpack. PAK: To go back to what you asked about what I would like to do, I really want to play a villain. PAK: Why don’t we join up and become super villains? NN:  I’m about to call Ryan Murphy right now and be like, ‘super villains, the both of us.’ PAK: ‘Paul and I got to talking, and we had this crazy idea…’ NN: I’m so happy I had this time to chat with you. I cannot wait to see you in Horror Story, and whatever else the universe has for you. And if we end up on set one day playing villains in the same project, somebody is gonna pull up this interview and be like, ‘how did this happen?’ And we’re gonna say we manifested it right now. Gordon Murray Special Vehicles debuted the S1 at Monterey Car Week, presenting a naturally aspirated supercar designed as a road-going tribute to the iconic McLaren F1. The new model serves as a refined counterpart to the track-focused S1 LM revealed in 2025. While the two vehicles share a carbon-fiber monocoque, the street-legal version features entirely bespoke bodywork and replaces aggressive fixed wings with an integrated active rear aero system. Under the rear clamshell sits a 4.2-liter Cosworth V-12 producing 680 horsepower and 368 pound-feet of torque. The mid-mounted powerplant utilizes titanium valves, titanium connecting rods and silicon carbide-coated lightweight pistons to safely achieve a staggering 12,100-rpm redline. Engineers tuned the motor to deliver 80 percent of its peak torque at just 2,500 rpm for improved everyday drivability. Buyers receive a six-speed manual transmission as the sole gearbox option, complete with straighter cable routing to enhance shift feel. The engine bay also visually honors its 1990s predecessor by incorporating a polished Inconel exhaust setup surrounded by a 24-carat gold-plated heat shield. To transform the hardcore platform into a capable touring machine, the engineering team increased the ride height by 10 millimeters and softened the suspension setup to maximize mechanical grip. The exterior design incorporates traditional dihedral doors equipped with standard roll-down glass rather than the fixed Lexan windows found on the LM variant. It rides on a staggered wheel setup featuring 19-inch front and 21-inch rear alloys wrapped in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires, with stopping power provided by cross-drilled Brembo brakes. Inside the cabin, the signature three-seat central driving position remains intact but gains thicker seat padding, enhanced sound insulation and a specially designed lightweight audio system. Founder Gordon Murray stated the special projects division exists to execute unique commissions that deviate from the rigid engineering formulas of the standard product lineup. Production is capped at 64 examples globally, marking a significant increase from the five-unit run of the LM. It's vital that Celtic take a positive result over to Linz the following Tuesday, with positive for being a win of any sort. Haissem Hassan, Mika Baur & Camilo Duran of Celtic. Celtic Training and press conference, photo Stuart Wallace IMAGO/ Shutterstock Celtic is absolutely flying at the moment, and that's all down to our attacking prowess, which has been greatly strengthened due to the signings of Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran with Haissem Hassan also been added to that list after signing from Real Oviedo last week. Our defence is also starting to look more solid and secure than it was last year, which is in a massive way down to the return of the highly influential Cameron Carter-Vickers. Kieran Tierney was rested at Tannadice with this game in mind and at right-back Anthony Ralston could come in to replace the less experienced Colby Donovan. Celtic manager Martin O'Neill watches on. Celtic Training and press conference, photo Stuart Wallace IMAGO/ Shutterstock Martin O'Neill may be considering a curve-ball of playing with a back three with Liam Scales joining CCV and Auston Trusty. That would push the two full-backs further up the field and help Celtic negotiate a potential problem area for this tie. Celtic's midfield is an area that could be something of a concern heading into both play off clashes. Paulo Bernardo was allowed to depart on loan, whilst Arne Engels has just signed for West Ham, and let's not forget that Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is suspended, meaning we are heading into the tie very light in the midfield department. Celtic's new signing Mika Baur poses in full Celtic home kit. Celtic Training and press conference, photo Stuart Wallace IMAGO/ Shutterstock That leaves us with just Callum McGregor, Mika Baur, Reo Hatate, Luke McCowan, and Benjamin Nygren to take on the Austrians. Each of the aforementioned names have their own abilities, and are terrific footballers, but none of them are what you would call an all round energetic midfielder, someone with a bit of dig as well as pace. Arne Engels gave us that trait, even if it was often overlooked, but now he's gone we don't possess that quality. That's concerning when you study the LASK midfield, an area that's arguably their greatest strength. + Brazil-focused copper and gold exploration company Prospectiva Resources has started trading on the TSX-V under the ticker 'PSVA'. The Toronto-headquartered company is advancing a portfolio of 100%-owned projects in the Borborema Belt. As Prospectiva enters the public markets, it is well positioned to create value through a fully funded drill programme starting this month, which is designed to expand the historical high-grade and near-surface copper/gold mineralisation at the São Francisco project. The programme will test newly identified electromagnetic conductors across a 3-km-long prospective geological and geophysical trend. The company has appointed ServDrill as the contractor, which has already mobilised to site. Notable historical high-grade intercepts from São Francisco include 7.5 m of copper grading 6.41% and gold grading 0.36 g/t, 4.5 m of copper grading 5.81% and gold grading 0.48 g/t, and 7.5 m of copper grading 3.83% and gold grading 0.36 g/t. The company holds another 335 km2 land package that hosts a pipeline of earlier-stage regional gold targets. While São Francisco is the company's primary focus, it is also advancing these earlier-stage targets, with first-pass geological reconnaissance having been completed at the Pico do Jabre and Desterro gold projects in the State of Paraíba - about 30 km north-east of São Francisco, comprising geological mapping, sampling of historical and active artisanal workings, as well as reconnaissance rock samples. Prospectiva says it is committed to executing a disciplined exploration strategy focused on systemic exploration and target advancement, with the aim of defining a mineral resource estimate next year. This will be achieved with an experienced leadership and technical team with a proven track record of mineral discovery and project development in Brazil, which Prospectiva deems to be a stable mining jurisdiction with established infrastructure and an efficient permitting framework. title: Cadillac V-One concept debuts at the Quail in California - Automotive World
content: “Our goal is to help stakeholders understand the future of mobility.” Home › News › Cadillac V-One concept debuts at the Quail in California The Quail debut gives Cadillac's V-One a public audience that equates performance authenticity with what it sees in real competition The Cadillac V-One concept is a single-seat, race-derived study rooted in the brand’s LMDh programme and co-developed with chassis constructor Dallara, translating V-Series.R prototype engineering into a driver-focused bespoke vehicle. The concept shares suspension components, transmission and select electronics with the V-Series.R race car and features a hybrid V-8 powertrain delivering 830 combined horsepower. The concept draws on the V-Series.R’s competition record across the IMSA WeatherTech Championship and FIA World Endurance Championship since 2023, comprising 10 wins, 16 pole positions and 32 podiums. That record includes the 2025 Le Mans Hyperpole and Cadillac’s first 1-2 finish in the World Endurance Championship at São Paulo. In a statement, Dominic Najafi, Executive Design Director, Global Cadillac, said: “The Cadillac V-One concept is the ultimate manifestation of a customer performance concept and is a clear sign of our ambition for the Cadillac V-Series brand in the future.” The exterior carries the V-Series.R’s proportions directly from the race car, with a new V-Series wheel design, updated dark-persona badging and a hand-sprayed paint gradient from silver to deep navy. Inside, the single-seat cabin blends exposed carbon structure with a bespoke, race-inspired interface and personalised materials. The V-One was unveiled at The Quail, A Motorsports Gathering in Carmel, California on 14 August 2026. Cadillac describes the concept as the first single-seat expression of the V-Series performance legacy and a clear statement of intent for the V-Series brand’s future direction. title: Nevada flags to fly at half-staff Monday to honor fallen firefighting pilot Christopher V. Andersen - FOX5 Vegas
content: CARSON CITY (FOX5) — Gov. Joe Lombardo has ordered flags at the Nevada State Capitol and all state public buildings and grounds to fly at half-staff Monday, Aug. 17, 2026, in honor of U.S. Forest Service-contracted helitack aerial firefighting pilot Christopher V. Andersen. Andersen died Aug. 7 while supporting aerial firefighting operations on the Widemouth 2 Fire near Three Creeks Reservoir in Fishlake National Forest, Utah. Co-pilot Mike Elliott, 50, also died in the crash of their Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane. MORE ON FOX5: A helicopter battling a Utah wildfire crashes as a blaze kills dozer operator in Oregon Andersen served five years as a helicopter pilot in the U.S. Army, including missions along NATO’s borders during the Cold War. Following his military service, he became a helitack pilot, helping protect communities threatened by wildfires throughout the American West and abroad. He made his home near Lake Tahoe, where he served as a chief pilot and mentor. Lombardo said Andersen earned the respect of fellow aviators for his skill, leadership, and professionalism. “Christopher V. Andersen dedicated more than four decades of his life to aviation and public service, first as a helicopter pilot in the U.S. Army and later flying critical missions and protecting communities across the country and around the world,” Lombardo said. “His courage, service, and dedication to protecting others will not be forgotten by the people of the State of Nevada.” The flag order applies to the Nevada State Capitol and all state public buildings and grounds from sunrise to sunset on Monday, Aug. 17. The order was issued at the request of Andersen’s family. Lombardo signed the proclamation Aug. 14, 2026.

title: Liverpool V Como: Match Review - The Anfield Wrap
content: by Neil Atkinson | Aug 16, 2026 | app, Featured, Featured Writing, Footie, Match Review | 0 comments It’s a long day. A game at 11:30am and a game at 6pm, Jacquet couldn’t have asked for it to have gone any better. He’s bright on the ball and emphatic off it. He senses danger and looks to love defending but he can clearly play. His goal is a lovely back post tap in that a number 9 would be delighted with. He looks like he has been worth waiting for. That, allied with Ronald Araujo’s second-half, means that suddenly centre-back looks the least of Liverpool’s concerns. Araujo is all action; he looks to win any loose ball and that eagerness could prove his undoing. But ultimately he just looks like a real boy and I like that. I like a footballer who looks frisky, who loves the battle, and there will be games where that is a huge bonus. It is a weight off. We’d all start Jacquet against Newcastle but if it has to be Araujo, or a burst of Araujo, then brilliant. It’s funny – Liverpool don’t seem to have signed a bad player for an extended period of time but we have squad concerns. Jeremie Frimpong today reasserts that. He sets up the opener by being direct and confident and playing a marvellous ball and then he defends excellently when the pressure is on for the rest of the first-half. Frimpong is a player about whom there are so many opinions but for me he is just a good attacking right back who actually anticipates danger well. What he can do about the danger from time to time is somewhat up in the air but he isn’t a dope, isn’t a winger, isn’t an oddity. The man who set Jacquet up for that goal was set up by Frimpong for his own. Cody Gakpo has now had two excellent performances in this pre-season. He looks the part, frankly. We’re in a funny position where Liverpool clearly want an exceptional left winger who – in my view – would prove worth the likely fee. But that doesn’t mean strength in depth should have its nose turned up at it. Gakpo is a proven Premier League winner and today he looked like that. At times he didn’t last year. But at times loads of them didn’t last year and indeed, at times we forget they are Premier League winners. Premier League winners in goal, at centre-back, in centre-mid and then a Bundesliga winner up top alongside Alexander Isak. There’s been too much of a desire to forget their class and pedigree. Lots of things don’t look perfect in terms of numbers and in terms of profile. Today there are gaps in the heart of the midfield again at times but when the building is on fire Liverpool at least man the buckets and that helps. Como show the ability to find space and play around corners and a side with more penetration could hurt The Reds. The truth of the situation is nuanced: Liverpool still don’t look quite ready for the start of an arduous campaign. There remains holes at the base of the midfield, especially when Nyoni isn’t on the pitch, which in and of itself begs questions. They look a top attacker down and look cover attackers down. They look off it at set pieces and they don’t progress the ball as well as you’d like through passing. But they look vibrant, ready to pose problems and look like they have goals in the them. Plus there is a key facet here – how does everyone else look? Only Arsenal appear to have most things in hand. Everyone else still has question marks somewhere. And it is these teams that we play starting from next weekend. The thing is, in the short term, we are talking about games. 90 minutes to get the points out of. Last season Liverpool progressively looked like they hated games, the very idea of playing blood and thunder football or coming up against it looked unconscionable to them. It turned their stomach. I’ve been at all the pre-season games (which is weird isn’t it? Should be locked up) and I have seen a Liverpool that wants to play and play. That starts next weekend and I don’t think we are ready. But I think we fancy it. I think we want it and welcome it. I don’t think our opponents are ready either and while they are at home, we know enough to know how that can be used against a side. I’m up for it and into it and I back us to score and I back us to hurt a side. Let’s start there. Two games until the window closes. Five games before the first break. Let’s find a path to eleven points. Won’t be easy. Isn’t impossible. Far from it. I’ve been to all five pre-season games and I have seen enough to be able to delude myself, to perhaps even be genuinely hopeful. You start with delusion. You get to hope. Then you can believe. content: Premier League champions Arsenal take on FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday. The curtain-raiser to the Premier League season takes place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, relocated from its usual home at Wembley due to a series of concerts by The Weeknd at the London venue. Follow the action from the Community Shield with our live blog here Arsenal won their first league title for 22 years when they finished top of the pile in May, seven points clear of Pep Guardiola's City, and Mikel Arteta will hope to pick up where they left off as they bid to defend their crown. City, who beat Chelsea 1-0 in the FA Cup final, begin a new era under Enzo Maresca after a decade of success led by Guardiola – although the club begin the new season with the threat of possible sanctions still hanging over them. Arsenal take on Manchester City at 3pm BST today, Sunday 16 August, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. The game will be broadcast live on TNT Sports in the UK. Subscribers can watch online via the HBO Max app and website. The Gunners will start the new campaign without key centre-back William Saliba after the France international suffered a back injury during the World Cup. Jurrien Timber is also injured and his return is "weeks away", according to Arteta. Manchester City are without Rodri, who underwent minor back surgery at the end of July after captaining Spain to World Cup glory. Abdukodir Khusanov missed the recent friendly against Atletico Madrid for personal reasons. But both sides are likely to be understrength as a result of key players resting following the World Cup. For City, Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi, Nico O'Reilly, new signing Elliot Anderson, Rayan Cherki and Jeremy Doku have only recently returned to training and are unlikely to start the game. For Arsenal, Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Mikel Merino, David Raya and Martin Zubimendi are in a similar position, with only a few days' training under their belts. Breton of Randolph, Maine, passed away peacefully on Aug. 13, 2026, leaving behind a legacy of faith, family, friendship, service, and adventure. Born on April 11, 1950, in Augusta, Richard lived a life rich with purpose and filled with the people and passions he loved most. After graduating from Cony High School, Dick married his high school sweetheart. In 1969, he joined the Army National Guard, where he proudly served for six years. He built a successful career in the grocery industry, beginning at Mister Market. He later joined Cottle’s Supermarket, working his way up to Store Manager, and continued his career with the company—now known as Hannaford—for 38 years. Dick enjoyed camping with his three daughters and, later, with his six grandchildren. He loved traveling with his wife and their special friends, and he especially cherished riding his Harley. He looked forward each year to motorcycle trips with his nephew Randy and their group of riders who affectionately called themselves the “Mild Hogs.” A man of deep faith, Richard was a member of St. Michael’s Parish in Augusta and a former choir member at St. Augustine Church. His lifelong love of music brought joy to his life and to all who knew him. He was a member of the Augusta Rotary Club for 13 years and served as President for one year. He especially enjoyed playing Santa at the annual Rotary Children’s Christmas Party. Richard was also a member of the Knights of Columbus Abnaki Council #334 and Le Club Calumet, and he served on the Festival de la Bastille committee for several years. During the Christmas season, he found great fulfillment in ringing the bell for the Salvation Army. Richard maintained an active lifestyle throughout his life. He enjoyed tennis, pickleball, golf, and kayaking adventures with the love of his life, Linette. Together, these snowbirds created countless treasured memories in both Maine and Florida. Dick was predeceased by his parents, Napoleon and Florence Breton; sisters Theresa Tardiff, Anita Martin and Yvette Breton, and brother, Eugene “Blackie” Breton. Above all, Richard was a devoted family man. He is survived by his wife of 57 years, Linette; his three daughters, Christine Devine (Christopher), Amy Perkins (Fred), and Allison Gallagher (Ron); his sister, Pauline Pelton; and his beloved grandchildren, Derek (and his wife Kayleigh), Jordan, Kyle, Nate, Casey, and Megan. One of Richard’s greatest joys was spending time with his grandchildren. He was also blessed to be a great-grandfather to Oliver and Remy. Richard celebrated each milestone of his growing family with love and unwavering support. He will be remembered for his warm smile, generous spirit, and his gift for making everyone feel welcomed and valued. To Richard, no one was ever a stranger. His memory will forever be cherished by his family and friends. A Mass of Christian Burial and celebration of Richard’s life will be held on Friday, Aug. 21 at 10 a.m. at St. Augustine Catholic Church, 75 Northern Ave., Augusta. Interment will follow at Holy Family Cemetery. The family would like to extend heartfelt gratitude to the staff at Andwell Hospice House for the support and kindness shown during this difficult time. Arrangements have been entrusted to Plummer Funeral Home, 16 Pleasant St., Augusta. title: What’s For Dinner? v. 21.07: It’s Pepper Season! Braised pork with peppers, Swordfish with red pepper aioli, and more… - Daily Kos
content:
This content is not subject to review by Daily Kos staff prior to
			publication. A few Christmases ago some foodie friends sent us a very nice Italian cookbook (see below), with a note in the front about their favorite recipe in the book. It quickly became a favorite of ours, too. It features a mix of peppers – sweet and spicy – so I decided August would be a relevant time to present this recipe along with a couple other things we love to do with peppers. This makes a good dinner for two plus leftovers, and I have always found I haven’t left enough peppers for the second time, so consider increasing the amount (weighed, one time, at 14 oz after coring and trimming and all). We have cooked with the peppers we have, not the specific ones the recipe wants us to have, which we have not yet hunted down. I serve this over soft polenta, pouring/spreading the extra polenta onto a small, oiled tray to chill and fry up the next day. The book in fact suggests making the pork and peppers a day ahead and reheating to bubbling. We have never considered waiting that long 😉 Chop the onion, rosemary, garlic, and anchovies together into 1/4-inch pieces. Coat a 12″ skillet lightly with EVOO and heat over med-high, then add the peppers, plus salt and freshly ground black pepper. Toss lightly to sear for about 2 minutes, then remove. Add a bit more oil to that in the pan, and when it is hot, add the pork, salt and pepper it, and brown well on all sides for about 10 minutes, taking care that “the glaze on the bottom of the pan” does not burn. Halfway through, add the bay, and a minute or two later, the chopped onion mixture, and finish browning the pork over medium heat, making sure to stir enough that the garlic does not burn, while the onion becomes golden brown. Add the vinegar. Simmer it “down to nothing” while scraping up the glaze from the pan. Add back the peppers, plus the water and tomatoes. Adjust the heat and let the liquid bubble slowly, covered, 50 minutes or till the pork is tender, stirring occasionally. Check the seasoning and serve, or refrigerate overnight and reheat to bubbling the next day. Serving over soft polenta is recommended. This is from The Italian Country Table, by Lynne Rossetto Kasper I love grilling/roasting peppers! Red sweet peppers are especially good roasted. You can buy jarred, roasted red peppers if you do not have a grill, but you can also roast them in the oven, I am told, or under a broiler – but not too close. The important thing when roasting your own peppers is to roast them whole, turning as each side gets blackened (just the skin, not the flesh). All the time the peppers spend in the hot oven or over the grill (covered!) the whole peppers are roasting, and this time is essential for them to be done right. Then you put the peppers into a heat-resistant container, where they will sort of steam themselves for about 15 minutes. After that, rub off the outer skins, seed and stem the peppers, and you have a delicacy on your hands. Place in a food processor two medium red peppers roasted as above, peeled, stemmed, and seeded, with 1 Tbsp olive oil and about 3/4 tsp salt [original: 1 tsp – my notes say too much; YMMV depending on your use of the sauce.] This recipe is infinitely useful, but it has a specific origin in Weber’s book Real Grilling, in a recipe called “Eggplant, Prosciutto, and Mozzarella ‘Sandwiches’.” You grill oiled, half-inch-thick slices from a globe eggplant – two per “sandwich” – one on both sides till done (maybe 4 minutes on a side on medium) and the other only on its first side. Turn the half-done slice so it is uncooked-side down, top with a Tbsp [or more] red pepper sauce, then a folded slice of prosciutto, a slice of fresh mozzarella, and then basil and the doubly-cooked eggplant on top. Grill, covered, till the bottom eggplant is fully cooked and the cheese is softened. With your food processor running, drop in two roughly chopped garlic cloves and run till minced. Add two red peppers, as above, grilled, peeled, stemmed and seeded, plus 3 Tbsp fresh lemon juice. Puree. In a small bowl, combine the puree with 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/4 tsp Kosher salt, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Keep refrigerated if you’re not using it immediately, but return to room temperature for the recipe that follows. This aioli recipe is from Weber’s Art of the Grill, in a recipe called “Swordfish Kabobs with Roasted Red Pepper Aioli.” OMG this is so good. One probably both cannot and should not have it often, due to the price and possible mercury accumulation in swordfish, but as an occasional treat, perhaps one could be forgiven. The original recipe is for 2 pounds skinless swordfish, which is a lot – my notes say 1 lb worked for three of us. So I make half the recipe and serve any leftovers for lunch the next day. These are the original amounts, for 2 lb fish. Cut the swordfish into 1 1/2″ cubes, and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes in a mixture of 3 Tbsp olive oil, 2 Tbsp freshly squeezed lemon juice, 1 Tbsp paprika (“preferably Hungarian”), and 1 tsp each chili powder and Kosher salt. Skewer the swordfish and grill over direct, medium heat, turning occasionally, until just opaque, about 5-6 minutes total (covered, always). My notes say, “Jasmine rice went with it perfectly!” The fish is excellent on its own, and so we served it to my father-in-law, who hated peppers, suggesting he try the aioli. He marveled to himself that he was going back for seconds of peppers! You’re getting all my favorite cookbooks in this diary (well, not all, they wouldn’t fit). This is from Pintxos, by Gerald Hirigoyen. Piperade is the kind of all-purpose recipe relegated to the “ingredients” section in the back of the book. Slice one small onion thinly, lengthwise. Core, seed, and cut into lengthwise strips 1 red and 1 yellow sweet pepper. Thickly slice (or crush) 6 peeled garlic cloves. Core and cut into ~ 3/4″ cubes four ripe tomatoes (I measured this to be about a pound). I use my monster 12″ Revere frying pan for this. Heat the pan over med-high, then add 1/3 cup olive oil and when it ripples, add the onion, peppers, garlic, and tomatoes. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally (or more often) “until the vegetables have softened and have begun to color.” Remove from the heat and allow to cool, then stir in Piment d’Espelette – my notes say 1 tsp worked – and Kosher salt, perhaps a generous version of 1/2 tsp. This stores in the fridge up to 5 days. First off, this works just as a condiment beside an omelette, sausage, good cheese, meat or fish, or whatever you like. Omelette: Mr pixxer cooked up three eggs with a bit of milk, S&P, then added raclette (a great melty cheese) and at the end, some piperade. He jerks the pan to flip over the omelette. I have never been that brave. Pizza! I tried using up leftover piperade once in a pizza, and I loved it. Mixed mozzarella and parmiggiano, more of the former than the latter, put 2/3 of it onto a slightly pre-baked pizza crust, spread piperade over it, and topped with the rest of the cheese. Easy! Sandwich: Just put it on a sandwich with cheese or whatever else you make sandwiches with. Not peanut butter. Piperade-braised beans with baked eggs: This is a classic, and the recipe is originally from Pintxos. Using the 3 cups (one recipe) of piperade above, 2 cups chicken or veal stock, and 2 cups dried cannellini beans (picked over, rinsed, soaked, drained), plus a 2-oz piece of smoked ham, and two choricero peppers (YMMV – I have not found this particular type), cook the beans for 1 or 1 1/2 hours, or till tender but not mushy. The chef has you discard the ham and choricero peppers but I would for sure eat the ham 🙂 Let cool to “warm”* and preheat the oven to 400. This is enough for six servings, but we make only two of the following, and have the rest reheated later without the eggs. Fill oven proof dishes each with about 1/6 of the bean mixture, make a well in the center of each, and break an egg into it. Place on a rimmed baking sheet or on the oven rack if you are confident you will not spill anything. Cook about 15 minutes, or until the whites are cooked, but the yolks are still soft. Sprinkle with salt and some parsley and serve. [*I have found that you need the beans pretty warm for the egg to cook effectively in them. The beans will be either insulating or cooking the bottom of the eggs.] Here’s one last, lovely pepper recipe from Martha Stewart. This is a GREAT potluck dish in that it’s easy to mix at the last minute. Opposing that…. well, if the definition of “gift item” is “something that looks more expensive than it is,” perhaps the definition of “potluck contribution” should be “something that looks harder than it is.” This is not that, simply b/c it takes a lot of time to cut everything carefully. But then, it’s so beautiful! What’s for Dinner? is a Saturday evening get-together where friends share recipes, talk about good food and help others answer culinary questions. title: Cadillac unveils V-One Concept Hypercar for the street - The Detroit News
content: Here’s a stoplight drag race we’d like to see at a future Woodward Dream Cruise: the Porsche 963 RSP vs. the Cadillac V-One. At Carmel, California’s summer autopalooza last week, The Quail, General Motors Co.'s luxury brand unveiled the wicked-looking V-One Concept based on the Cadillac V-Series.R hypercar that endurance-races across the globe from Daytona to Le Mans. The V-One comes a little over a year after Porsche’s street-legal hypercar — also based on their Le Mans endurance racer — debuted at the 2025 24 Hours of Le Mans in France. The car was gifted by Porsche to Roger Penske, Porsche’s partner in international sports car racing. Like the 963 RSP (short for Roger Searle Penske), the V-One is a street-focused version of the V-Series.R. The two cars are likely the fastest street-legal vehicles ever conceived. Unlike the Porsche, Cadillac hailed the V-One as a halo for future V-Series brand design. “The Cadillac V-One Concept is the ultimate manifestation of a customer performance concept and is a clear sign of our ambition for the Cadillac V-Series brand in the future,” said Global Cadillac Executive Design Director Dominic Najafi before the silk was pulled off the new Caddy. Development of a production car from a race car is hardly new at GM. The current Corvette C8 Z06, for example, was developed alongside the Corvette GT3.R race car that also competes in international sportscar racing. The Z06 shares the same high-revving, dual-overhead can V-8 engine as the race car. Unlike the Corvette, however, which sells 25,000-35,000 units a year, the V-One Concept would be a rare vehicle if produced. “It’s about as close to the race car as you can get,” says Sean O’Shea, Cadillac Hypercar Propulsion Manager. V-One is a notable departure from recent Cadillac concepts that had electric powertrains (the Opulent Velocity, Solleim and InnerSPace). The addition of the V-One to Cadillac’s halo arsenal alongside those concepts and the hand-built Celestiq EV indicates the continued co-existence of electric and V-8s within the brand. Not only does V-One boast an eight-cylinder engine prized by Dream Cruisers like the CT5 V-Series Blackwing road car — but it is also a hybrid. Cadillac does not sell a hybrid vehicle. “At the heart of the V-One is a V-8 hybrid powertrain that shares foundations with the Cadillac V-Series.R race car, underscoring the concept’s serious capability and authenticity,” said the Cadillac press release of the electrified, 5.5-liter V-8. Under 37 mph, the race car operates on the electric motor before the V-8 roars to life leaving the pit lane. That duality is likely shared by the V-One. While V-One shares the race car’s earth-shaking powertrain, it possesses significantly more power: 830-horsepower versus 670 for the V-Series.R due to so-called Balance of Performance racing regulations to encourage close racing between brands as varied as Cadillac, Porsche, Ferrari, BMW, Aston Martin, etc that compete in Hyeprcar racing with their own production-derived powerplants. That is also true of the Corvette Z06 which produces 670 horsepower (the highest of any normally-aspirated production car) versus 500 for the GT3.R. Other elements of the V-One closely track the race car including its carbon-fiber monocoque chassis made by the Dallara race shop in Italy, high-downforce aerodynamics, and sophisticated suspension. They also appear to share track-focused Michelin Pilot Sport slicks. Where the V-One departs from its sibling is in its premium detailing — notably a striking silver-to-night paint job (the race car gets a vinyl wrap) and luxurious cockpit materials. The interior is made with recycle materials, carbon-fiber trim, and a more comfortable driver’s seat (while still holding the driver in at a neck-straining 3 Gs at, ahem, 150 mph). The steering wheel is less complicated and bears a screen. “The interior of the car is one of the main selling points with the car," said O’Shea. “You open the doors and you look inside and it's a clean, purpose-built race car with a bespoke Cadillac interior.” The intention to make the car more utilitarian (the V-One engine, assures Cadillac, doesn’t require “a team of specialists just to operate”), but its track roots are still a priority. Cadillac says, despite the added luxury and weight, V-One should lap withing 10% of V-Series.R times. A serialized plaque on the door teases Cadillac’s intention to make more copies for sale. Perhaps as a garage partner to the also- limited edition, hand-built Celestiq EV. “(V-One) is a serious machine, but it’s amazing how we’ve been able to bring this curated design element to it to make it feel like a very special car,” said Nafaji. “The Celestiq represents ultimate luxury, the V-One represents ultimate performance.” Henry Payne is auto critic for The Detroit News. Find him at hpayne@detroitnews.com or Twitter @HenryEPayne.
